Cyclist Magazine Podcast: Phil Cavell on the Cycling Addiction

This week on the Cyclist Magazine Podcast, James is joined by the bicycle polymath himself, Phil Cavell. Cyclist, bike-fitter, author, writer, speaker, racer, shop owner, bike designer, wrench and generally very clever bloke, Phil, together with friend and long-term business partner, Julian Walls, helped pioneer bike-fitting back in the early 2000s, opening Europe’s first dedicated bike-fit studio, CycleFit, in London on 2003.

Over the years, Phil has worked with top pros from the Trek team and a young Tom Pidcock, as well as amateurs from all walks of life. But whoever they are, they are all concerned with one thing – staying fit and getting the best out of cycling a bike.

Phil has written numerous articles for Cyclist magazine – we are a real paper magazine you can buy in a real shop, and our latest issue is out now! – but more importantly, he’s penned several books, the most recent of which, The Cycling Addiction (Bloomsbury), we discuss today. Concerning ‘suffering, speed and the search for meaning on two wheels’, The Cycling Addiction seeks to discover what it is that draws us to such a punishing sport, and what functions of the mind, body and evolution are responsible for cyclists producing extraordinary feats of endurance, even to the point of death.

But this isn’t just a chat about the physiology. Phil talks about his own experiences and others’ from a philosophical and emotional point of view, including the idea that cycling for some is a mechanism of control, an identity anchor and a self-esteem booster. Who hasn’t got a little tingle opening Strava and seeing a new gold medal?

Chat begins at 6:17.

The Cycling Addiction by Phil Cavell is out now, published by Bloomsbury.
